summary: Intermittent 401 on token refresh in Private deploy — Authorization header stripped by egress proxy on retried HTTP/2 streams
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on Private deployment intermittently see 401 Unauthorized errors during token refresh flows. The errors are observed only from SDKs that reuse long-lived HTTP/2 connections (stream multiplexing), and only when the client retries the token-refresh request after a 401/401->retry sequence.

Impact:
- Token refresh failures cause transient auth lapses for control-plane API calls and artifact downloads, resulting in model load failures and degraded inference requests for a subset (~2-4%) of sessions.
- Affects Valence HealthTech's private VPC deployment in us-east-1; incident window 2026-03-01 03:00–10:30 UTC.

Environment:
- Redwood Private deployment (customer-managed egress) in us-east-1
- SDK: redwood-sdk-go v0.9.12 and redwood-js v2.3.1
- Serving runtime: 2026-02-14 build
- Egress path: customer NGFW -> corporate HTTP/2 reverse proxy -> outbound NAT

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Long-running client establishes HTTP/2 connection to control-plane (token endpoint).
2) Access token expires; SDK issues POST /v1/tokens/refresh using same pooled connection.
3) Initial refresh attempt receives 401 from control-plane (valid case if token already revoked), SDK retries refresh after short backoff reusing same HTTP/2 connection.
4) Second request arrives at corporate proxy but Authorization header is missing on the retried request. Control-plane rejects with 401 and client starts a cascade of retries or fails the request.

Logs & snippets:
- Client side trace (timestamped): "POST /v1/tokens/refresh stream-id=5 -> 401; retry stream-id=9 missing Authorization"
- Control-plane access logs show second request with empty Authorization header and x-forwarded-for preserved.
- tcpdump from a serving node (pcap excerpt) shows Authorization present on bytes for the first stream, absent on the second.

Initial hypothesis:
- Egress proxy or NGFW is performing HTTP/2 stream-level inspection and rewriting that drops sensitive headers on retried streams or strips headers when connection-level state indicates a new stream without a fresh header frame.

Workaround (temporary):
- Customer configured the SDK to disable HTTP/2 connection reuse (force HTTP/1.1) which eliminated the intermittent 401s.

2026-03-02 11:30 UTC — Eng (Maya Patel): Confirmed SDK HTTP/2 retry uses new stream id but relies on connection-level header continuation; proxy rule matched and removed 'Authorization' on subsequent streams. Preparing mitigation patch for SDK to always include credentials on retry. Reference PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821
2026-03-03 14:05 UTC — Customer: Applied temporary workaround to force HTTP/1.1 in SDK; observed no more 401s during 24h smoke tests.

2026-03-05 09:45 UTC — Support (Ava): Deployed SDK patch v0.9.13 with explicit Authorization-on-retry; requested customer to revert HTTP/2 change and monitor. Customer confirmed stable. Closing follow-up monitoring in 48h.
2026-03-05 10:30 UTC — Customer (Valence SRE): Verified revert and stability; no errors in 72h. Thanks for quick turnaround.
investigation_notes: Captured full pcap from serving node and from customer egress gateway during incident window; compared Authorization header bytes across initial and retried streams.

Reproduced behavior in lab by standing up corporate-proxy v3.2.7 with header-filter rules that drop sensitive headers on non-first stream frames; reproduction confirmed only for HTTP/2 multiplexed connections.

Hypothesis validated: proxy's header-filtering module considered retries as "new transactions" and stripped Authorization unless the request carried explicit per-request headers (some frameworks rely on implicit continued headers via connection reuse).

Customer proxy vendor (AceroProxy) notes: default security profile includes 'suppress-auth-on-subsequent-streams' to prevent credential replay across multiplexed clients; option is configurable in profile 'strict-reuse-block'.

Tested two mitigations: 1) configure proxy to allow Authorization passthrough for defined upstream (requires vendor change), 2) SDK change to always attach Authorization on every retry even when connection reused. SDK change was quicker to ship and minimally invasive.
resolution:
Root cause: customer egress proxy was stripping Authorization header on retried HTTP/2 streams due to a security profile setting ('suppress-auth-on-subsequent-streams'). Fix path: 1) short-term: shipped SDK update (redwood-sdk-go v0.9.13 and redwood-js v2.3.2) to attach Authorization header explicitly on retry attempts even when reusing HTTP/2 connections; 2) recommended long-term: customer to update proxy profile to allow passthrough for Redwood control-plane endpoints or add an allowlist for upstream token endpoints.

Action items completed:
- Deployed SDK patch and published release notes with migration guidance. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821)
- Customer reverted HTTP/1.1 workaround and monitored for 72h with no recurrence.
- Internal INT-1124 opened to track proxy rule guidance and add a knowledgebase article.

Follow-up:
- Create KB article for private-deploy customers describing known proxy profiles that strip per-request headers on multiplexer protocols and recommended patterns. (Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/5643/egress+proxy+policy+runbook)
- Consider SDK telemetry that warns when retries occur over HTTP/2 without explicit per-request headers.
